channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: Lula migrou do Nordeste para São Paulo, liderou movimentos sindicais e pode chegar a 16 anos como presidente do Brasil
item.description: Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, the incumbent president and 2026 re-election candidate, is seeking a fourth term, which would bring his total time in office to 16 years, second only to Getúlio Vargas. Born in Pernambuco and raised in São Paulo from childhood, Lula built his career in the labor movement and is married to Janja da Silva, having faced multiple health challenges during his presidencies, including surgeries and cancer treatments. His ticket features Geraldo Alckmin as vice president, confirmed by the PSB.

item.title: Campanha de Haddad aposta em temas nacionais e na privatização da Sabesp para levar eleição ao segundo turno
item.description: Fernando Haddad's campaign for São Paulo governor is focusing on the privatization of Sabesp, the Trump administration's tariffs, and national sovereignty to gain votes and push the election to a runoff. Campaign coordinators believe Tarcísio de Freitas has left gaps in his support, with dissatisfied mayors and legislators, and expect to gain momentum in the final stretch.

item.title: Novo aciona TSE contra Lula e aliados por suposta propaganda eleitoral antecipada em convenção do PT na Bahia
item.description: The Novo party filed a representation with the TSE against Lula, Jerônimo Rodrigues, Jaques Wagner, Rui Costa, and the PT, alleging premature electoral propaganda during the PT's Bahia convention on June 1. The action requests the removal of event videos from digital platforms, arguing that Lula made explicit vote requests before the official campaign start date of August 16.

item.title: Ao pedir votos para a suspeição, Lula afronta a lógica, a lei e a PF
item.description: Lula urged votes for PT candidates in Bahia, including Jaques Wagner, who is under investigation for ties to the now-defunct Banco Master, on the eve of the convention that will formalize his bid for a fourth term. The move was criticized for defying logic, the law, and the Federal Police, given Wagner’s suspected misconduct. The statement constitutes an explicit appeal for support for a figure under scrutiny, sparking controversy over ethics and impartiality.

item.title: A internação da ex-primeira-dama Michelle Bolsonaro
item.description: Former First Lady Michelle Bolsonaro announced she is hospitalized in Brasília due to a persistent headache lasting over ten days, which prevented her from attending the launch of Bia Kicis’s Senate campaign. She confirmed she will run for one of the two Senate seats from the Federal District, forming a 'pure-blood' ticket with Bia Kicis, both from the PL party, after being persuaded by Governor Celina Leão and Senator Damares Alves.

item.title: O Brasil e o mundo rejeitam Trump (por Mary Zaidan)
item.description: The Pew Research Center reveals Donald Trump as the least trusted U.S. president in history, with 76% negative global approval and 81% rejection of his tariffs in Brazil. In the 2026 Brazilian electoral context, foreign policy has gained attention not for its intrinsic importance, but due to the Bolsonaro clan’s missteps in aligning with Trump and Javier Milei, which has benefited Lula and harmed Flávio Bolsonaro. Genial/Quaest will measure the impact of these external influences, including Michelle Bolsonaro’s reconciliation with her stepson and the AI appearance of Jair Bolsonaro at the PL convention.

item.title: Novo vai ao TSE contra Lula após pedidos de voto em convenção do PT
item.description: The Novo party filed a complaint with the TSE against President Lula, Bahia Governor Jerônimo Rodrigues, and Senators Jaques Wagner and Rui Costa, all from the PT, over alleged premature electoral campaigning during the party's state convention in Bahia. The filing requests, on an urgent basis, the removal of videos showing explicit calls to vote for the PT candidates. Novo claims these acts violate electoral law by constituting campaign activity before the legally permitted period.

item.title: Eleições 2026: entenda as 7 mudanças nas regras de doações
item.description: The Superior Electoral Court approved Resolution TSE nº 23.752/2026, modernizing donation rules for the 2026 General Elections. Key changes include dispensing with electoral receipts for Pix donations (while retaining donor identification), enabling digital opening of campaign bank accounts, maintaining the ban on cryptocurrencies, and reinforcing transparency and inclusion through specific criteria for allocating FEFC and Party Fund resources to indigenous, women, and Black candidacies.

item.title: Estarei na campanha de Flávio “de uma maneira ou de outra”, diz Tereza Cristina
item.description: Senator Tereza Cristina (PP-MS) stated she will participate in Flávio Bolsonaro's (PL-RJ) presidential campaign 'one way or another', despite her party, the PP, deciding not to formally support the candidate. The remark was made during the União-Progressista Federation convention in Mato Grosso do Sul. Tereza Cristina had previously indicated willingness to run as vice-president on the Bolsonaro ticket.

item.title: História do voto: mulheres do RN tiveram feitos inéditos
item.description: Rio Grande do Norte was a pioneer in women's suffrage in Brazil and South America with state law nº 660 of 1927, which guaranteed voting rights to women without sex distinction. Celina Guimarães Viana was the first woman to register as a voter and vote in the country in 1928, followed by Júlia Alves Barbosa Cavalcante. Alzira Soriano de Nóbrega Teixeira became the first elected female mayor in Brazil and Latin America that same year, winning a campaign marked by misogynistic attacks.

item.title: Conquista do voto feminino no Brasil resistiu à misoginia histórica
item.description: Women's suffrage in Brazil was achieved after decades of misogynistic resistance, with discourses questioning women's political capacity resurfacing in 2026 despite being clearly unconstitutional. Experts state these manifestations violate Articles 14 and 5 of the 1988 Federal Constitution, constituting discrimination and potential criminal acts, and emphasize that rights require permanent struggle. Despite historical progress, patriarchal structures persist, demanding institutional vigilance to protect universal suffrage.

item.title: Poder de reação: como funciona a nova lei que permite uso de spray de pimenta
item.description: The federal government has sanctioned a law allowing women to use pepper spray as a non-lethal self-defense measure, in response to rising feminicide rates and public security concerns. The law restricts purchase to adults over 18, limits canisters to 50 ml, and permits use only in moderate, proportional response to physical or sexual attacks. Though initially hesitant, President Lula approved the measure to avoid confrontation with right-wing legislators ahead of the 2026 elections, despite reservations from security experts.

item.title: Virou palanque: em uma eleição polarizada, candidatos disputam a cadeira de secretário-geral da ONU
item.description: The race to succeed António Guterres as UN Secretary-General is polarized between former Chilean president Michelle Bachelet, backed by left-wing governments like Brazil and Mexico, and Argentine Rafael Grossi, IAEA director supported by the right and endorsed by Javier Milei. The process, held in New York, unfolded amid a weakened UN marked by Security Council divisions and financial strain, with the final decision depending on behind-the-scenes negotiations among permanent and rotating members through October.

item.title: Ao vivo: PL realiza convenção estadual na Paraíba
item.description: The Liberal Party held its state convention in Paraíba on Sunday (August 2, 2026), in João Pessoa, with the presence of Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ), the party’s presidential candidate. The event launched Senator Efraim Filho (PL) as the gubernatorial candidate and former Health Minister Marcelo Queiroga (PL) as the Senate nominee, reflecting the Bolsonarist strategy to expand influence in the Northeast, a region traditionally dominated by the Workers’ Party (PT).

item.title: O canto da sereia: o esforço dos presidenciáveis para tentar seduzir o setor produtivo
item.description: In 2002, Lula overcame the productive sector's distrust by releasing the 'Letter to the Brazilian People,' committing to maintain economic policy pillars, which secured his election and re-election. In 2026, heterodox proposals by Sergio Gabrielli, PT's government program coordinator, sparked market concern, prompting the government to deploy Dario Durigan and Fernando Haddad to convey economic credibility and counter the fallout. The strategy aims to win over business leaders and avert a projected fiscal collapse from 2027 onward if public spending is not controlled.

item.title: Deputado aciona PGR após Lula pedir votos na Bahia
item.description: Federal deputy Sanderson (PL-RS) filed a complaint with the Attorney General's Office (PGR) against President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) after the president urged votes for himself and allies during a PT party convention in Bahia. The complaint alleges that the statements may constitute premature electoral propaganda, as they occurred before the official start of the 2026 election campaign.

item.title: A frase de Napoleão que orienta a estratégia de Lula contra Flávio Bolsonaro
item.description: A Lula advisor cited a quote attributed to Napoleon Bonaparte to justify the strategy of not directly attacking Flávio Bolsonaro, arguing that the president should wait for his main rival to make mistakes before acting. The statement was made in response to questions about Lula’s alleged lack of offensives against the Bolsonaro candidate. The content is marked as subscriber-only, requiring registration for full access.

item.title: Conheça as 4 empresas que produziram as urnas ao longo de 30 anos
item.description: Since 1996, Brazil's Superior Electoral Court (TSE) has overseen the production of electronic voting machines, with 14 models and 1.487,115 units manufactured by four companies selected through bidding: Positivo Tecnologia, Diebold/Diebold Procomp, Unisys Brasil, and Procomp Indústria Eletrônica. The machine's design is fully defined by the TSE, with over 500 pages of technical and security requirements, and its manufacturing process is audited by Electoral Justice officials, ensuring a nationally developed and state-owned voting system.

item.title: O último encontro a sós entre Lula e Fachin já tem mais de duas décadas
item.description: Supreme Court Justice Edson Fachin, who completed one year as president of the STF in August, has never had a private meeting with President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva since the start of Lula’s third term — unlike other justices who reportedly seek frequent audiences with the presidency. His stance is noted for rigorously upholding the separation of powers, avoiding any appearance of closeness that could undermine judicial independence.

item.title: PT faz convenção nacional neste domingo para confirmar candidatura de Lula à reeleição
item.description: The Workers' Party (PT) will hold its national convention on Sunday, August 2, at Expo Center Norte in São Paulo, to officially nominate President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva for re-election in 2026, alongside Vice President Geraldo Alckmin (PSB). The event takes place just before the TSE's August 5 deadline and will feature top leaders from allied left and center-left parties. Lula leads in all voter intention polls and will face his main opponent, Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ), son of former president Jair Bolsonaro, who is currently imprisoned for attempting a coup d'état.

item.title: Convenção do PL volta a exibir vídeo com voz atribuída a Bolsonaro
item.description: The PL convention displayed a video featuring a voice attributed to Jair Bolsonaro while confirming Jorginho Mello’s re-election bid as governor of Santa Catarina, despite objections from Supreme Court Minister Alexandre de Moraes regarding the use of such material.

item.title: Por que aliados acham que Lula não recebe Alcolumbre
item.description: Lula's allies believe the anticipated meeting with Senate President Davi Alcolumbre will not happen — and likely never will — because Lula reportedly possesses sensitive information about Alcolumbre's alleged involvement in the Master scandal and Daniel Vorcaro's affairs. Avoiding the encounter is seen as a way to prevent legitimizing someone perceived as implicated in corruption.

item.title: Lula busca reeleição sob a sombra de Trump
item.description: At 80, Lula launched his campaign for a fourth presidential term in 2026, positioning himself as a defender of Brazilian sovereignty against Donald Trump’s U.S. policies. He emphasized the need for national independence amid global geopolitical tensions.

item.title: Lula e Lulinha, vai dar no quê?
item.description: The Federal Police investigation into Fábio Luís Lula da Silva, known as Lulinha, raises concerns about its potential impact on President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva’s 2026 re-election bid. A poll of 1,042 readers found that 28.7% believe the investigation could harm his father’s candidacy, while 71.3% disagree. The case underscores the political sensitivity of family members’ legal entanglements during electoral campaigns.

item.title: Infra em 1 Minuto: corrida da IA é disputa de capacidade de geração de energia
item.description: CBIE partner Pedro Rodrigues argues that global AI leadership will be determined less by model sophistication and more by electricity generation capacity, emphasizing China's lead due to its massive coal-powered electricity output despite being a top renewable exporter. Brazil, despite having an 87% renewable energy matrix and abundant resources, fails to attract AI investments due to excessive regulation and restrictions on natural gas and nuclear power, prioritizing ideological energy choices over pragmatic ones.

item.title: Entenda de onde vem o dinheiro das campanhas eleitorais
item.description: The 2026 Brazilian electoral campaigns are funded through multiple sources, including the Electoral Fund (nearly R$ 5 billion for 30 registered parties), the Party Fund, candidates' and parties' own resources, individual donations via digital 'vaquinha virtual' platforms, and revenue from events and product sales. These funds can cover expenses such as campaign propaganda, graphic materials, event space rentals, candidate transportation, campaign committees, staffing, and sound trucks. The TSE oversees financing by requiring specific bank accounts, electoral receipts for all funds received, and full transparency—prohibiting banking secrecy and allowing unspent public funds to be returned to the National Treasury.

item.title: O Judiciário está mais ativista?
item.description: The article argues that the Brazilian judiciary is not becoming more activist, but rather that there has been a reconfiguration of the state's power distribution: Congress has expanded its legislative and budgetary role, including the execution of amendments, while the STF has taken on a coordinating role, establishing transparency norms in response to fragmented parliamentary decisions. This new dynamic reflects a 'progressive parliamentaryization of spending,' with the judiciary acting as an institutional coordinator amid the lack of centralized planning in resource allocation.

item.title: A saúde como política industrial: o que muda com a sanção do PL 2583/20
item.description: President Lula signed PL 2583/2020 into law, establishing the National Strategy for the Health Economic-Industrial Complex (Ensceis), which transforms discretionary SUS procurement practices into a stable legal framework to strengthen national production of strategic health inputs. The law defines technical categories such as Strategic Health Product (PES) and Critical Technological Component (CTC), and creates the Strategic Health Company (EES), accredited by the Executive, to integrate SUS purchasing power with reindustrialization policies and reduce external technological dependence.

item.title: Céu de brigadeiro para Tarcísio e tempo fechado para Flávio
item.description: Lula is preparing for his seventh and possibly final presidential run in 2026 at age 80, with the possibility of resigning in 2030 to run for the Senate. Meanwhile, Flávio Bolsonaro, son of former President Jair Bolsonaro, was overlooked at the Republicanos convention that nominated Tarcísio de Freitas for re-election as governor of São Paulo, receiving support mainly from the PL, while Tarcísio enjoys backing from a coalition of 12 parties.

item.title: Além de Trump: eleição brasileira será marcada por pressões externas
item.description: The 2026 Brazilian presidential election is unfolding under intense external pressure, with the United States, China, and the European Union shaping the political landscape through sanctions, economic partnerships, and ideological alignments. Experts note that, for the first time since redemocratization, the race is embedded in a global geopolitical contest, transforming Brazil from a passive observer into a strategic actor. President Lula warned of possible interference by the Trump administration to support Senator Flávio Bolsonaro, a pre-candidate for the presidency.

item.title: Convenção em SP é estratégia de Lula focando maior colégio eleitoral
item.description: Lula will be officially confirmed as the re-election candidate at a convention this Sunday in São Paulo, targeting the country's largest electoral college with over 34.1 million voters. The choice of São Paulo reflects the PT's strategy to reverse its 2022 defeat, when he lost to Bolsonaro by nearly 2.7 million votes in the state. The event will also confirm Geraldo Alckmin as his running mate.

item.title: Milei e onda azul na América do Sul desafiam liderança regional de Lula
item.description: Despite Lula's efforts to revitalize South American integration through the Brasília Consensus, his regional leadership faces challenges due to ideological divergences, diplomatic crises, and the rise of the 'Blue Wave' in the region, led by figures like Javier Milei in Argentina. The antagonism between Lula and Milei reflects a broader conflict between left-wing and right-wing governments, affecting institutional cooperation and Brazil's regional leadership.

item.title: O futuro em jogo
item.description: Since 1989, approximately 40% of Brazilian voters have consistently voted against Lula in presidential elections, with peaks during the candidacies of Collor and Aécio Neves. Bolsonaro’s emergence intensified this anti-Lula base with violent rhetoric — both physical and verbal — and antidemocratic conduct, deepening national polarization. The article frames this division as a historical and enduring political phenomenon.

item.title: TSE regulamenta aplicativo para relatar propaganda irregular
item.description: The TSE has regulated the Pardal Móvel app to enable citizens to report irregular electoral propaganda in the 2026 elections, accessible via e-Título or Gov.br with identity protection guaranteed. The tool, consisting of three modules (Pardal Móvel, Pardal ADM, and Pardal Web), will be available from August 16 and features automated case classification, media attachment support, and protocol generation for tracking.

item.title: PP lança Celina ao GDF e PL faz convenção esperando reencontro de Michelle e Flávio
item.description: Celina Leão, governor of the Federal District and PP candidate for re-election, officially launched her campaign with support from PP, União Brasil, Republicanos, MDB, Podemos, and possible PL endorsement, with Gustavo Rocha (Republicanos) as her running mate for vice-governor. The PL held its convention with anticipation of a public reunion between Michelle Bolsonaro (former first lady) and Flávio Bolsonaro (senator and presidential candidate), following their social media reconciliation, with Michelle confirmed as the PL’s Senate candidate for the DF. Bia Kicis was also confirmed as the PL’s Senate candidate for the Federal District.

item.title: ‘Deepfake’ de Bolsonaro usado pelo PL em convenção divide ministros e obriga TSE a delimitar regras sobre IA
item.description: The use of a deepfake of Jair Bolsonaro by the PL party at a convention to support Flávio Bolsonaro’s candidacy has divided TSE ministers and prompted the court to establish new rules on AI use in elections. While the TSE resolution bans deepfakes intended to deceive or attack opponents, there is disagreement over whether non-deceptive, supportive uses—like aiding candidate communication—are permissible. The article notes the AI-generated video simulated the former president’s voice to endorse his son.

item.title: Não há despolarização eleitoral, mas a divisão na vida social talvez esteja em grupo menor, avalia coordenador da pesquisa 'A Cara da Democracia'
item.description: Leonardo Avritzer, coordinator of the 'A Cara da Democracia' research, states that although electoral polarization remains intransigent, tolerance in personal relationships suggests it may be confined to a minority group in Brazilian society. Over half of respondents said they fully tolerate relationships with people of opposing political views, indicating a possible easing of polarization in social life, even as it persists in the electoral sphere.

item.title: Apesar polarização eleitoral, maioria dos brasileiros é tolerante com quem pensa diferente, aponta a pesquisa ‘A Cara da Democracia’
item.description: Despite electoral polarization, most Brazilians show tolerance in personal relationships with those who hold opposing political views, according to the 'A Cara da Democracia' survey. While 45% dislike Bolsonaro supporters and 35% reject PT supporters, only about 20% are considered more intolerant in concrete situations like dating, friendship, or family unions. Researchers note that political division does not translate into significant social rupture, unlike in the United States.

item.title: Novo perde espaço de partido antissistema e vê Renan Santos se contrapor a Zema
item.description: The Novo party is betting on Romeu Zema’s presidential pre-candidacy to reclaim its liberal and anti-system electorate, distancing itself from Bolsonarism. In the race for this same voter base, the Missão party, led by Renan Santos, launched its candidacy with the 'Yellow Book', advocating similar platforms such as a minimal state, ending racial quotas, and criticizing the STF. Novo aims to leverage Zema’s campaign to regain national strength after its 2022 electoral decline, which resulted in loss of party fund access and free TV time.

item.title: Lula prepara convenção discreta e mira largada da campanha no ABC
item.description: President Lula will attend a low-key PT convention in São Paulo this Sunday, aiming not to overshadow his official campaign launch on August 16 in the ABC region. The event will emphasize short speeches and broad allied party support, contrasting with the PL’s mega-event that featured international figures and saw audience drop-off. The PT expects 3,000 attendees at the convention, compared to a projected 30,000 for the August 16 rally.

item.title: Naskar: empresário usou namorada para dar golpe em empresa da família Zema
item.description: Douglas Azara, owner of the fintech Naskar, used his girlfriend, lawyer Jessika Lorrane Bastos de Castro, her brother and his grandmother to orchestrate a scheme that diverted R$75 million from Zema Financeira, a company linked to the family of former Minas Gerais governor and presidential candidate Romeu Zema, between November and December 2025. The Minas Gerais Civil Police traced the fraudulent operations to the couple's residence in Anápolis (GO), where Jessika provided logistical support, her bank accounts and a sole proprietorship to facilitate the illicit fund flow. Azara is currently a fugitive in Dubai, flaunting luxury assets, while Jessika is also wanted with a pending preventive arrest warrant, despite her OAB-GO registration remaining active.

item.title: Com Inter x Corinthians, confira jogos da Copa do Brasil deste domingo
item.description: The Copa do Brasil resumes this Sunday with four first-leg round of 16 matches, starting with Palmeiras vs Fortaleza at 4 p.m., followed by Mirassol vs Grêmio at 6 p.m., Chapecoense vs Cruzeiro at 6:30 p.m., and the highlight: Internacional vs Corinthians at 7:30 p.m. at Beira-Rio. The matches come after the 2026 World Cup break and determine the first qualifiers for the quarterfinals, with return legs scheduled for Wednesday and Thursday of next week.

item.title: Michelle amplia influência no PL após crise com Flávio, banca aliados e provoca incômodo em diretórios estaduais
item.description: Michelle Bolsonaro expanded her influence in the PL following Flávio Bolsonaro's public apology, solidifying her role as an arbiter in bolsonarist internal disputes. She directly shaped candidacies, protected allies, and interfered in state-level agreements, such as in the Federal District, where she maintained PL support for Governor Celina Leão and sidelined Senator Izalci Lucas. Her Senate candidacy for PL-DF is expected to be confirmed at the party convention this Sunday, marking her first meeting with Flávio since the video controversy.

item.title: Deterioração das estatais agrava crise fiscal
item.description: The financial health of Brazil's state-owned enterprises is deteriorating, according to a report by the Independent Fiscal Institution (IFI) linked to the Senate, which shows that the consolidated primary financial result fell from a surplus of 0.2% of GDP in January 2020 to a deficit of 0.07% in May 2026. Even at the start of President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva's term, the balance was still positive at 0.06% of GDP, indicating that the decline occurred during his administration. The situation reflects a worsening fiscal crisis tied to the management of state-owned companies.

item.title: Caiado diz que Lula e Flávio brincam de “esconde-esconde” em debates
item.description: Ronaldo Caiado accused Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro of avoiding presidential debates, describing the situation as a 'hide-and-seek' where each conditions their appearance on the other's. He advocated for a confrontation based on concrete management data, criticizing Lula's alleged superficiality in speeches and questioning Flávio Bolsonaro's lack of administrative experience.

item.title: Vox Brasil: gestão Tarcísio é aprovada por 65,3% dos paulistas
item.description: The Vox Brasil Institute poll shows that 65.3% of São Paulo residents approve of Governor Tarcísio de Freitas' administration, while 29.1% disapprove and 5.6% did not express an opinion. In the stimulated scenario, Tarcísio leads with 52.9% of voting intentions, followed by Fernando Haddad at 34.3%, suggesting a potential first-round victory.

item.title: Tarcísio marca 52,9% e venceria Haddad no 1º turno, aponta Vox Brasil
item.description: A Vox Brasil poll shows Governor Tarcísio de Freitas (Republicanos) would be re-elected in the first round with 52.9% of voting intentions, ahead of Fernando Haddad (PT) at 34.3%. In a simulated runoff, Tarcísio leads with 53.5% versus Haddad’s 35.8%, or 59.9% of valid votes. Haddad is the most rejected candidate at 47.5%, while Tarcísio has 24.3% rejection.

item.title: Lula lança sétima candidatura e faz tira-teima com a História
item.description: Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva launches his seventh presidential campaign today. After three initial defeats (1989, 1994, 1998), he won in 2002, 2006, and 2022, now seeking to cement his political legacy in a 'test with History'.

item.title: PT lança neste domingo, em SP, candidatura de Lula à reeleição
item.description: The Workers' Party (PT) officially launched President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva's re-election bid for 2026 at its national convention in São Paulo on Sunday. Lula, aged 80, will seek a fourth presidential term, running again with incumbent Vice President Geraldo Alckmin (PSB) as his running mate. The coalition includes PSB, PCdoB, PV, PDT, PSOL and Rede, while main rival Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) has yet to announce alliances.

item.title: Zema acusa Lula de "ilícito eleitoral" por pedir voto: "Um intocável"
item.description: Romeu Zema (Novo) accused President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva of committing electoral illicit by asking for votes before August 16, during a PT convention in Bahia. Zema criticized the Supreme Federal Court (STF), suggesting it was in coalition with the PT, and pointed out that Lula refers to Jaques Wagner as Senate government leader despite Wagner being under investigation by the Federal Police for allegedly receiving R$ 3.5 million and a luxury apartment from Banco Master’s owner. Zema also noted he himself is under investigation for a video using puppets to simulate dialogues between STF ministers.
